_comment: Read by .github/scripts/check_test_suites.py after every Unity test leg.
allowedNonPassing: the only Ignored, Skipped, Explicit or Inconclusive results a leg may report and stay green.
Every other one fails it, because the runner counts none of them as failures and a green leg would then
mean less than it says. 'test' and 'message' are fnmatch globs over the test-case's fullname and its
reason message. 'when' / 'unless' name a condition the workflow passes per leg: expectsAudio (the leg's
image promises a realtime audio device) or randomOrder (the leg ran with -randomOrderSeed).
An entry needs a reason. Adding one is a decision to let a test not run, so make it narrow.
minimumFixtures: floors under the fixture derivation, to catch a source scan that stopped seeing the
suite. Deliberately far below the real counts - they are not a second inventory.

allowedNonPassing.reason: Editor Addressables in 'Use Asset Database' mode can complete a load synchronously, in which case the mid-load window the test is named for does not exist on that machine. The test Assumes the window rather than re-proving the synchronous path.

RequireRealtimeAudioClock ignores a test when the DSP clock is not realtime, which is right on a machine with no audio device. Where the image promises one, AudioClockProbeTests fails the leg and this entry does not apply, so each gated test that was skipped is reported too.
B_, D_ and E_ check what the fixture restored after A_ or C_ mutated it, and Assume their predecessor ran first. A random order can run them before it; they then say so rather than pass vacuously.
